summary.title: SecureNova AI Identity Security - Prebuilt Draft
summary.description: Threat model for SecureNova Inc.'s AI-powered customer service platform. Covers human and non-human identities, Auth0/OIDC, OAuth M2M, LLM credentials, AI agent orchestration, RAG, vector storage, MCP tools, internal REST APIs and centralized security monitoring.

cells.description: External customer who authenticates through Auth0 and submits customer-service requests.
Identity provider for OIDC/OAuth authentication, token issuance, MFA, RBAC and identity lifecycle management.
cells.privilegeLevel: Identity platform administrator; customer and service token issuance

threats.title: Identity Provider Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker may redirect authentication traffic to a fraudulent identity provider or exploit weak issuer validation, causing users or services to trust attacker-controlled identity assertions.
threats.mitigation: Pin the trusted issuer and discovery configuration; validate issuer, audience, signature, nonce and state; use TLS and approved redirect URIs.

threats.title: Authentication Policy Modification
threats.description: An attacker with excessive administrative access may alter Auth0 application, connection, MFA or authorization settings.
threats.mitigation: Restrict tenant administration, require MFA for administrators, review configuration changes, use change control and monitor tenant logs.

threats.title: Authentication Event Dispute
threats.description: Insufficient identity-provider audit records may prevent investigators from determining who changed settings or authenticated a principal.
threats.mitigation: Export Auth0 logs to centralized tamper-resistant storage; retain actor, timestamp, client, IP, event and outcome fields.

threats.title: Token or Profile Data Exposure
threats.description: Access tokens, refresh tokens or customer profile attributes may be exposed through logs, browser storage or misconfigured applications.
threats.mitigation: Never log secrets or bearer tokens; use secure storage, TLS, short token lifetimes, least-data scopes and redaction.

threats.title: Authentication Endpoint Flooding
threats.description: Automated login or token requests may exhaust authentication capacity or trigger service disruption for legitimate users.
threats.mitigation: Enable brute-force protection, suspicious-IP throttling, rate limits, bot detection, alerting and recovery procedures.

threats.title: Auth0 Administrator Privilege Abuse
threats.description: A compromised or over-privileged administrator or client may modify identity policies or grant excessive API scopes.
threats.mitigation: Apply least privilege to tenant roles and M2M clients, separate duties, require MFA and periodically review grants.

cells.description: LLM-powered agent that processes customer requests, calls the LLM, retrieves knowledge through RAG and invokes approved MCP tools.

threats.title: AI Agent Identity Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker may impersonate the legitimate AI agent using stolen service credentials, forged identity claims or replayed tokens to access internal resources.
threats.mitigation: Use workload identity, short-lived service tokens, cryptographic token validation, secure credential storage and identity monitoring.

threats.title: AI Agent Instruction Manipulation
threats.description: Malicious user input or retrieved content may manipulate agent instructions and cause unintended tool calls or data changes.
threats.mitigation: Separate trusted instructions from untrusted content, apply prompt-injection defenses, validate tool arguments and enforce server-side authorization.

threats.title: AI Agent Activity Repudiation
threats.description: Missing or incomplete agent activity records may prevent attribution of tool calls, data access or consequential actions.
threats.mitigation: Log user and agent identities, request IDs, timestamps, tool names, authorization decisions and outcomes to tamper-resistant storage.

threats.title: AI Agent Customer Data Exposure
threats.description: The agent may expose customer data, secrets or internal context in generated responses, prompts or external model requests.
threats.mitigation: Apply data minimization, PII detection and redaction, retrieval authorization, output filtering and restrictions on external data sharing.

threats.title: AI Agent Resource Exhaustion
threats.description: Excessive requests, oversized prompts or repeated tool calls may exhaust agent, model or downstream service resources.
threats.mitigation: Apply rate limits, token budgets, request-size limits, timeouts, concurrency caps, quotas and abuse monitoring.

threats.title: AI Agent Privilege Escalation
threats.description: A manipulated or compromised agent may invoke tools or APIs beyond its approved scope or inherit excessive user permissions.
threats.mitigation: Use least-privilege delegated scopes, tool-level authorization, server-side checks, separation of duties and human approval for sensitive actions.

cells.description: Machine-to-machine OAuth client that obtains scoped access tokens for approved service-to-service API calls.
cells.privilegeLevel: Specific API audience and least-privilege scopes

threats.title: M2M Client Credential Theft
threats.description: An attacker may obtain a machine-to-machine client secret and impersonate the OAuth client.
threats.mitigation: Store secrets in a secrets manager, rotate them, restrict access and prefer private-key or workload-based client authentication where supported.

threats.title: M2M Client Configuration Tampering
threats.description: An attacker may modify redirect, grant, audience or scope configuration to weaken client security.
threats.mitigation: Restrict configuration changes, use change review, monitor administrative events and apply configuration-as-code controls.

threats.title: M2M Client Activity Attribution Gap
threats.description: Missing client and token issuance logs may prevent attribution of automated API activity.
threats.mitigation: Log client ID, subject, audience, scopes, token issuance events, request IDs and API outcomes.

threats.title: M2M Secret Exposure
threats.description: Client secrets or access tokens may leak through source code, CI logs, environment dumps or application logs.
threats.mitigation: Use managed secret storage, secret scanning, short-lived tokens, redaction and rotation after suspected exposure.

threats.title: M2M Token Request Flooding
threats.description: Automated token requests may exhaust rate limits or impair legitimate service authentication.
threats.mitigation: Apply client-specific rate limits, cache tokens safely until expiry and alert on anomalous token issuance.

threats.title: Excessive M2M API Scopes
threats.description: An OAuth client may be granted broad scopes that allow access to unrelated or privileged API operations.
threats.mitigation: Grant only required scopes, separate clients by workload, review grants regularly and enforce audience-specific authorization.

cells.description: External model endpoint that receives approved prompts and context and returns generated responses.
cells.privilegeLevel: Provider-side model inference; no direct enterprise API authority

threats.title: LLM Endpoint Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker may redirect the application to a fraudulent model endpoint and receive prompts or sensitive context.
threats.mitigation: Use approved provider endpoints, TLS certificate validation, allow-listing and configuration integrity checks.

threats.title: LLM Request or Response Manipulation
threats.description: Requests or responses may be altered in transit or by an untrusted intermediary.
threats.mitigation: Use TLS, validate provider endpoints, integrity-protect application configuration and validate structured outputs.

threats.title: LLM Request Attribution Gap
threats.description: Insufficient request identifiers and provider-side records may prevent investigation of model requests and responses.
threats.mitigation: Record request IDs, model/deployment, caller identity, timestamp, policy decision and response metadata without logging secrets.

threats.title: Sensitive Prompt Context Exposure
threats.description: Customer data, secrets or internal documents may be sent to an external model provider without appropriate controls.
threats.mitigation: Minimize prompt data, redact PII and secrets, review provider data terms, restrict retention and use approved data-processing settings.

threats.title: LLM Quota or Availability Exhaustion
threats.description: Excessive calls or provider outages may exhaust quotas or interrupt AI service responses.
threats.mitigation: Apply request budgets, rate limits, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, fallback handling and usage alerts.

threats.title: Model Tool-Use Boundary Bypass
threats.description: Model output may be treated as authorization to perform actions, allowing untrusted generated content to trigger privileged tools.
threats.mitigation: Never treat model output as authorization; enforce independent policy checks and scoped tool permissions in the application.

cells.description: Managed storage for LLM API credentials and service secrets; access is restricted to approved workloads.
cells.privilegeLevel: Secret retrieval only for authorized workload identities

threats.title: Secret Store Accessor Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker may impersonate a workload authorized to retrieve LLM API credentials.
threats.mitigation: Use workload identity, strong authentication, narrow secret policies and access reviews.

threats.title: Secret Rotation or Version Tampering
threats.description: An attacker may replace a stored API credential or alter its active version to redirect or disrupt model access.
threats.mitigation: Restrict secret write permissions, require approval for rotation, version secrets and audit all changes.

threats.title: Secret Access Audit Gap
threats.description: Insufficient access logs may prevent identifying which principal retrieved or changed an API credential.
threats.mitigation: Enable immutable secret access and administrative audit logs with principal, secret identifier, time and action.

threats.title: LLM API Key Exfiltration
threats.description: An attacker may extract an LLM API key from source code, runtime environment, logs or prompt context.
threats.mitigation: Keep keys in a secret manager, never place keys in prompts or logs, restrict retrieval, rotate exposed keys and monitor provider usage.

threats.title: Credential Availability Disruption
threats.description: Deletion, revocation or access-policy changes may prevent the application from obtaining a valid LLM credential.
threats.mitigation: Use controlled rotation, versioning, recovery procedures, alerts and tested break-glass access.

threats.title: Secret Read Permission Escalation
threats.description: A workload may gain unauthorized access to secrets belonging to other services or environments.
threats.mitigation: Use per-secret access policies, environment separation, least privilege and periodic permission reviews.

cells.description: Retrieval service that authorizes queries, retrieves relevant enterprise knowledge and returns approved context to the agent.
cells.privilegeLevel: Read approved knowledge sources; ingestion writes separately controlled

threats.title: RAG Service Identity Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker may impersonate the RAG service using stolen service credentials or forged tokens to access the knowledge store.
threats.mitigation: Use workload identity, short-lived tokens, issuer/audience validation, secure secrets and allow-listed service principals.

threats.title: RAG Document and Chunk Poisoning
threats.description: Malicious or altered documents and chunks may manipulate retrieval results and influence agent responses or tool decisions.
threats.mitigation: Validate source provenance, authorize ingestion, scan content, maintain hashes and versions, restrict write access and review changes.

threats.title: RAG Retrieval Audit Failure
threats.description: Insufficient logs of ingestion, retrieval and returned chunks may prevent reconstruction of suspicious knowledge access.
threats.mitigation: Record source document IDs, chunk IDs, query/request IDs, service identity, timestamps, ingestion changes and authorization outcomes.

threats.title: Unauthorized Knowledge Retrieval
threats.description: Weak document-level controls may allow the pipeline to return confidential documents or tenant data to unauthorized users.
threats.mitigation: Enforce document-level authorization and tenant filters before retrieval; redact sensitive data and apply least privilege to vector queries.

threats.title: RAG Retrieval Service Exhaustion
threats.description: Expensive vector searches, oversized queries or high request volume may exhaust retrieval resources.
threats.mitigation: Apply query limits, rate limits, timeouts, concurrency caps, quotas, caching and anomaly detection.

threats.title: RAG Service Privilege Escalation
threats.description: A compromised RAG service may gain write or administrative access to the vector database or restricted knowledge sources.
threats.mitigation: Separate read and write identities, use granular database roles, validate authorization server-side and monitor privileged operations.

cells.description: Stores embeddings, document chunks and metadata used by the RAG pipeline for semantic retrieval.
cells.privilegeLevel: RAG-scoped read; controlled ingestion and administration

threats.title: Vector Database Client Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker may impersonate an approved RAG client to query or modify indexed knowledge.
threats.mitigation: Require authenticated service identities, rotate credentials and validate client authorization on every connection.

threats.title: Vector Index or Embedding Modification
threats.description: An attacker may alter embeddings, metadata or indexed chunks to influence retrieval results.
threats.mitigation: Restrict write access, verify ingestion provenance, maintain versioned backups and monitor index changes.

threats.title: Untraceable Vector Queries
threats.description: Insufficient query and update logs may prevent attribution of sensitive reads or unauthorized modifications.
threats.mitigation: Enable audit logging for queries, writes, deletes, principal, tenant, timestamp and result metadata.

threats.title: Cross-Tenant Vector Data Leakage
threats.description: Missing tenant or document-level filters may return embeddings or chunks belonging to another customer or security domain.
threats.mitigation: Enforce tenant isolation and metadata filters server-side; test access boundaries and minimize returned fields.

threats.title: Vector Search Exhaustion
threats.description: Large or frequent similarity searches may exhaust compute, memory or database connection capacity.
threats.mitigation: Set query limits, quotas, timeouts, concurrency controls and capacity alerts.

threats.title: Unauthorized Vector Index Administration
threats.description: A service identity with excessive privileges may modify or delete indexes or access restricted collections.
threats.mitigation: Separate query and administration roles, apply least privilege and require approval for destructive changes.

cells.description: MCP server exposing approved tools and validating caller identity, tool permissions and arguments before execution.
cells.privilegeLevel: Only explicitly approved tools and scoped backend operations

threats.title: MCP Server Identity Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker may impersonate an MCP server or client using stolen credentials or forged authentication tokens.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate service-to-service connections, validate tokens, use workload identity and mutual TLS where appropriate, and rotate credentials.

threats.title: MCP Tool Invocation Manipulation
threats.description: An attacker may manipulate tool names, arguments or execution requests through prompt injection or compromised agent instructions.
threats.mitigation: Validate tool schemas and arguments, allow-list tools, enforce server-side authorization and require approval for sensitive operations.

threats.title: MCP Tool Execution Repudiation
threats.description: Missing tool invocation records may make it difficult to attribute an operation to a user, agent or service identity.
threats.mitigation: Log caller identity, user context, tool name, validated arguments, request ID, timestamp, authorization decision and result.

threats.title: MCP Sensitive Data Exposure
threats.description: Overly broad tool responses may expose customer records, internal information or secrets to an unauthorized caller.
threats.mitigation: Apply tool-level scopes, response filtering, field-level authorization, redaction and output minimization.

threats.title: MCP Server Resource Exhaustion
threats.description: Repeated or expensive tool invocations may exhaust MCP server capacity or downstream API quotas.
threats.mitigation: Use per-client rate limits, execution timeouts, concurrency limits, quotas, circuit breakers and monitoring.

threats.title: MCP Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
threats.description: Weak tool authorization or excessive service permissions may let an agent execute privileged operations beyond its approved scope.
threats.mitigation: Use least-privilege service identities, granular tool permissions, server-side authorization, scoped tokens and human approval for privileged actions.

cells.description: Enterprise API for customer records, orders and support operations; every operation requires authentication and object-level authorization.
cells.privilegeLevel: Endpoint- and object-level authorization; least privilege

threats.title: Internal API Caller Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker may use stolen service credentials or forged tokens to impersonate an authorized API client.
threats.mitigation: Validate issuer, audience, signature, expiry and scopes; use workload identity and short-lived credentials.

threats.title: Unauthorized Customer Record Modification
threats.description: An attacker may manipulate API parameters or request bodies to alter customer or order records.
threats.mitigation: Validate schemas, enforce object-level authorization, use integrity controls and log sensitive changes.

threats.title: Internal API Operation Repudiation
threats.description: Insufficient audit evidence may prevent attribution of customer-data reads or changes to a user, agent or service.
threats.mitigation: Create tamper-resistant audit events with principal, request ID, action, object, timestamp and outcome.

threats.title: Broken Object-Level Authorization
threats.description: An authenticated caller may access another customer's records by changing object identifiers or exploiting missing authorization checks.
threats.mitigation: Enforce object-level authorization on every request, minimize responses and test tenant isolation.

threats.title: Internal API Request Flooding
threats.description: High request volume or expensive operations may degrade internal API availability.
threats.mitigation: Use gateway rate limits, quotas, timeouts, circuit breakers and capacity monitoring.

threats.title: Internal API Scope Escalation
threats.description: A client may invoke administrative or sensitive endpoints using excessive or incorrectly validated scopes.
threats.mitigation: Use least-privilege API scopes, deny by default, enforce authorization at each endpoint and review service grants.

cells.description: Centralized security monitoring and tamper-resistant audit storage for authentication, agent, RAG, MCP and API events.
cells.privilegeLevel: Append-only audit ingestion; restricted log administration

cells.description: Customer authenticates with Auth0 over TLS using the configured OIDC flow.

threats.title: Credential Interception
threats.description: Credentials or authorization codes may be exposed if authentication traffic is not protected.
threats.mitigation: Require HTTPS/TLS, secure redirect URIs, PKCE where applicable and never transmit credentials over plaintext channels.

threats.title: Login Request Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker may initiate a deceptive login flow or exploit weak state/nonce validation.
threats.mitigation: Validate state and nonce, restrict redirect URIs and use approved OIDC libraries.

cells.description: Authenticated customer request and relevant customer-provided content are submitted to the AI application.
Auth0 issues an access token; the application validates signature, issuer, audience, expiry and scopes before use.

threats.title: OAuth Access Token Manipulation
threats.description: An attacker may alter token claims, scopes or identity attributes to gain unauthorized access to AI agent resources.
threats.mitigation: Validate JWT signatures and claims (issuer, audience, expiry); reject unsigned or invalid tokens and enforce scope checks.

threats.title: OAuth Access Token Exposure
threats.description: A bearer token may leak through logs, browser storage, insecure transport or debugging output, allowing unauthorized use.
threats.mitigation: Use TLS, secure token handling, short-lived access tokens, redaction and never log bearer tokens.

threats.title: Authentication Service Denial of Service
threats.description: Excessive authentication or token-validation requests may prevent legitimate users and services from obtaining or validating tokens.
threats.mitigation: Apply rate limits, brute-force protection, suspicious-IP throttling, anomaly monitoring and availability controls.

cells.description: Agent sends minimized prompt and approved context to the external model endpoint and receives generated output.

threats.title: Sensitive Prompt Context Exposure
threats.description: Sensitive customer or enterprise data may be sent to an external model without sufficient minimization or policy controls.
threats.mitigation: Redact secrets and PII, minimize context and use approved provider data-processing settings.

threats.title: Untrusted Model Output Manipulation
threats.description: Untrusted or malformed model output may influence downstream decisions or tool parameters.
threats.mitigation: Treat model output as untrusted; validate structured output and independently authorize actions.

cells.description: Agent requests relevant enterprise knowledge; the RAG service enforces caller and document-level authorization.
RAG service performs authorized similarity searches and receives approved document chunks and metadata.

threats.title: Unauthorized Vector Result Disclosure
threats.description: Missing tenant or document-level filters may return restricted chunks to an unauthorized caller.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side tenant and document authorization before returning results.

threats.title: Vector Search Result Manipulation
threats.description: Compromised index data or metadata may alter which chunks are returned.
threats.mitigation: Protect index writes, validate provenance and monitor index changes.

cells.description: Agent requests an approved MCP tool; MCP validates caller identity, tool authorization and argument schema before execution.

threats.title: MCP Tool Argument Tampering
threats.description: Tool parameters may be altered or crafted to trigger unintended operations.
threats.mitigation: Validate schemas and business rules server-side; reject unexpected fields and enforce authorization.

threats.title: Unauthorized Tool Invocation
threats.description: An agent may request a tool beyond the caller's approved permissions.
threats.mitigation: Enforce tool-level authorization and least-privilege scopes independently of model output.

cells.protocol: MCP transport with authenticated service identity

cells.description: MCP server invokes scoped internal REST API operations and receives operation results.

threats.title: API Scope or Object Authorization Bypass
threats.description: A caller may access endpoints or records outside its granted scope.
threats.mitigation: Validate scopes and object-level authorization on every endpoint and request.

threats.title: Sensitive API Response Exposure
threats.description: API responses may contain customer or internal fields not needed by the caller.
threats.mitigation: Apply response minimization, field-level authorization and redaction.

cells.description: Authorized runtime retrieves the LLM API credential from the secret store; credential is never placed in prompts or logs.

text.text: M2M client registration and token policy

cells.description: Auth0 maintains the machine-to-machine client registration, allowed audience and least-privilege scopes.

text.text: M2M access token and API request

cells.description: M2M client obtains a scoped token and invokes only the authorized API audience and endpoints.
API emits authentication, authorization, access and operation events to centralized audit storage.
Auth0 authentication, token issuance, administrative and anomaly events are forwarded for monitoring.
Agent emits request IDs, identity context, tool-selection decisions and outcomes without recording secrets or unnecessary PII.
MCP emits caller identity, tool name, validated argument metadata, authorization decision and execution result.
RAG emits document provenance, ingestion changes, retrieval identifiers and authorization outcomes.
